title: Ibrahim Zadran’s 95 powers Jaffna Kings to win over Colombo Kaps - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
July.29 (Mirror Sports) - Jaffna Kings boosted their Lanka Premier League 2026 playoff hopes with a convincing 19-run victory over Colombo Kaps at the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium, powered by Ibrahim Zadran’s brilliant half-century and Dilshan Madushanka’s match-winning bowling spell.

Zadran produced his best innings of the tournament, anchoring the Jaffna innings with a classy 95 from 65 deliveries. The Afghanistan opener combined timing and power, smashing 12 boundaries and three sixes before narrowly missing out on a well-deserved century.

Kamil Mishara provided valuable early momentum with 44, while Towhid Hridoy’s unbeaten 31 helped Jaffna finish strongly as they posted an imposing 202 for 5 from their 20 overs.

Colombo needed an aggressive start in their chase but struggled to build momentum throughout the innings. Sadeera Samarawickrama top-scored with 44, while Kamindu Mendis and Milan Rathnayake contributed 28 and 26 respectively. However, regular wickets prevented Colombo from building the partnerships required.

Madushanka turned the game decisively in Jaffna’s favour with an outstanding left-arm pace spell, claiming 3 for 30 — his best bowling figures of the tournament. He received strong support from the rest of the attack as Colombo’s required run rate continued to rise.

Colombo eventually finished on 183 for 9, handing Jaffna Kings another valuable victory as the race for the LPL 2026 playoffs intensifies.

Brief Scores:

Jaffna Kings 202/5 (20 overs): Ibrahim Zadran 95 (65), Kamil Mishara 44, Towhid Hridoy 31*; James Neesham 2/30.

Colombo Kaps 183/9 (20 overs): Sadeera Samarawickrama 44 (36), Kamindu Mendis 28, Milan Rathnayake 26; Dilshan Madushanka 3/30.

Result: Jaffna Kings won by 19 runs.

title: NARA investigates blue bottle jellyfish presence at Panadura beach - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 28 (Daily Mirror) - The National Aquatic Resources Research and Development Agency (NARA) has launched an investigation into the presence of Physalia, commonly known as the blue bottle jellyfish, along the Panadura beach and issued safety advice to the public following reports of several beachgoers being stung.

The investigation was initiated after the Panadura Municipal Council informed NARA about an increased presence of jellyfish in the coastal area. NARA officials visited the beach this evening to examine the situation, identify the species and assess potential risks to the public.

A NARA official said there is a high possibility that blue bottle jellyfish have washed ashore along the entire stretch of Panadura beach.

The move follows an incident yesterday in which several swimmers were affected by jellyfish stings while at Panadura beach. The victims were admitted to hospital, received treatment and were later discharged.

The blue bottle jellyfish is known for its painful sting, which in some cases can cause severe pain, allergic reactions and breathing difficulties.

NARA advised the public to exercise caution when entering the sea in areas where jellyfish have been reported and to follow safety instructions issued by relevant authorities.

title: Uganda declares end to latest Ebola outbreak - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Reuters - Uganda's health minister declared the country Ebola-free on Tuesday following the East African nation's latest outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic ‌disease that infected 20 people and killed two of them.

Uganda has suffered multiple outbreaks of Ebola since 2000, when it recorded its first epidemic, and officials say over the years the country gained expertise it has used to bring recent infections under control quickly with limited community spread.

Fifteen ⁠people in the latest outbreak, declared in mid-May, were infected in neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo - the epicentre of the epidemic, where the number of confirmed cases now stands at more than 3,000.

The last Ebola patient in Uganda, a Congolese national, was discharged on June 22. That is short of the 42-day waiting period required by the World Health Organization to declare the end of an outbreak.

But Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi said the announcement follows the "successful completion of ‌the ⁠mandatory 42-day monitoring period which begun after the discharge of the last Ugandan national, a locally transmitted patient, on the 16 of June, 2026."

Of the 20 confirmed cases during the outbreak, 18 were discharged while two died from the virus, both of ⁠whom were from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

"Throughout this period the ministry of health maintained intensive surveillance nationwide and no new Ebola cases have been detected," Baryomunsi said.

Officials say ⁠Uganda's many tropical forests that teem with fruit bats, which are natural reservoirs for the virus, make it vulnerable to frequent outbreaks.

The virus is transmitted ⁠through contact with infected bodily fluids and tissue and symptoms include headache, vomiting of blood, muscle pains and bleeding.

title: S&P says Sri Lanka’s Economy showing resilience, keeps rating stable - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 28 (Daily Mirror) - S&P Global Ratings has affirmed Sri Lanka’s long- and short-term sovereign credit ratings at ‘CCC+/C’, while maintaining a stable outlook, citing continued economic recovery, strong revenue growth and improvements in fiscal management.

The ratings agency said Sri Lanka’s economy has remained resilient despite multiple external challenges, with increased government revenue helping to support fiscal consolidation and reduce debt servicing pressures.

However, S&P warned that the country’s external position could come under pressure this year due to a higher import bill and possible impacts from the Middle East conflict on tourism earnings and worker remittances.

The stable outlook reflects S&P’s expectation that Sri Lanka’s economic growth and fiscal recovery will continue over the next six to 12 months, although external risks remain significant.

“Sri Lanka’s creditworthiness remains vulnerable and dependent on favourable financial and economic conditions, but the government does not face an immediate risk of a debt or payment crisis,” the agency said.

S&P noted that Sri Lanka’s economic recovery has been stronger than expected, with real GDP growing 4.8% in the fourth quarter of 2025 and 5.1% in the first quarter of 2026.

The agency expects economic growth to slow to 3.8% in 2026 due to higher energy costs and external pressures before recovering to 4.2% in 2027 as global energy conditions improve.

S&P highlighted that government revenue increased significantly, supported by tax reforms and economic recovery. Revenue rose by 34% in 2025 to 16.7% of GDP, while the fiscal deficit narrowed to 2.3% of GDP.

Revenue growth continued in the first five months of 2026, increasing by 30% compared to the same period last year, the agency said.

However, S&P cautioned that Sri Lanka’s external position has weakened due to rising imports, currency pressures and uncertainty over tourism and remittance inflows.

The ratings agency said the Middle East conflict could affect Sri Lanka through higher energy prices, reduced tourism earnings and slower remittance growth, as the region accounts for a significant share of foreign worker remittances.

It also warned that a stronger El Niño event in 2026 and 2027 could pose risks to agriculture, electricity generation and overall economic activity.

S&P said Sri Lanka’s continued commitment to reforms under the International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme, including improving government revenue, cost recovery in utilities and strengthening public financial management, would remain important for further economic improvement.

The agency said it could upgrade Sri Lanka’s ratings if stronger economic growth leads to further improvements in fiscal and external positions. However, the ratings could be downgraded if renewed funding pressures or a significant deterioration in economic conditions emerge.

title: Trump flouts political risk to host Netanyahu’s seventh White House visit - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
ALJAZEERA - United States President Donald Trump is set to host Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House for the seventh time during his second term, flouting the political risk of holding a high-profile meeting with the increasingly unpopular leader amid the US-Israel war with Iran.

The face-to-face on Tuesday will be the first time the two men have met since they jointly launched the war on February 28, a turn that has piqued the already growing wariness of Israel among the US public, and increasingly, within some segments of Trump’s own Republican Party.

The meeting was announced late last week, with Netanyahu already planning to travel to Washington, DC, for the funeral of US Senator Lindsey Graham, one of the staunchest supporters in Congress of Israel’s interests.

“There hasn’t been a Netanyahu visit since the war began, probably because the war so quickly devolved into a disaster that it just becomes bad optics to have Netanyahu come here,” Andrew Day, senior editor at The American Conservative, told Al Jazeera.

A slate of recent polls has shown Republican disapproval of US policy towards Israel growing, if still markedly less than among Democrats. Notably, a Politico poll released last week showed just a third of self-identified Make America Great Again (MAGA) voters, typically the most unquestioning of Trump’s base, felt the economic costs of the war with Iran were worth it.

Couple that with the widespread perception that Israel pulled the US into the war with Iran, Day said, and the meeting with Netanyahu could prove politically costly as Republicans stare down the midterm elections just over three months away.

“I don’t think Trump personally perceives the risks, although the risk definitely exists,” Day said.

The timing of Tuesday’s meeting is particularly notable, with Trump signalling on Monday that Washington was pursuing a new diplomatic overture with Iran.

That came after the dissolution of the June 17 memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the US and Iran, which had agreed to halt fighting on all fronts, leading to 13 consecutive days of escalation. The fighting has since been paused for three days.

Netanyahu’s government had vehemently opposed the MoU, arguing that it strengthened Tehran’s hand while yielding few concessions.

Israel has continued to push for wider regime change and a zero-tolerance policy towards Iran’s nuclear programme, in contrast to the Trump administration’s recent pursuit of off-ramps as it has sought to frame the conflict as a victory.

In June, Israeli operations in Lebanon, which threatened to derail the MoU, prompted a rare rebuke from Trump and US Vice President JD Vance, who has been the most outspoken critic of Israeli policies within the administration.

At the time, Vance warned Israeli government officials against criticising the Trump administration: “If I was in the cabinet of the Israeli government, I might not be attacking the only powerful ally that I have anywhere left in the entire world,” he said.

Speaking to reporters on Monday, Trump again made reference to the unequal relationship: “Frankly, we’re being very nice to a lot of countries that would not survive without us. And you know who wouldn’t survive without us? Israel.”

To be sure, Trump has regularly touted his continued support for both Netanyahu and Israel, and the rhetoric has not amounted to real policy change.

“Whatever criticisms the administration might have been making publicly or privately about Netanyahu, the policy hasn’t changed,” Matt Duss, the executive vice president of the Center for International Policy, told Al Jazeera.

Instead, he said Tuesday’s invitation to the White House reflects Trump’s enduring connection to the Israeli leader, despite the shifting sands of public opinion. No other world leader has met with Trump as many times as Netanyahu. Beyond the White House visits, the Israeli prime minister also met with Trump at his Mar-a-Lago estate in December 2025.

“Given that they’ve been so close, perhaps Trump just feels it would be too big of a story if he didn’t give him a meeting again,” Duss said.

That is not to say that the meeting will be inconsequential, he added. Netanyahu has in the past used such events to make personal appeals to Trump to further his war agenda.

“Netanyahu knows how to influence Trump,” Duss said. “And Trump can be very influenced by the last person he spoke to if that person knows how to speak to him in the right way.”

Netanyahu, for his part, has said Tuesday’s meeting would address several issues, “primarily Iran”.

“Of course, our goal is to protect our security and also to expand the circle of peace around us,” he said.

Compared to Trump, the benefits of the Oval Office are more clear-cut for Netanyahu, according to Michael Omer-Man, the Israel-Palestine director at the DAWN advocacy group.

Any face time with the US president could buoy Netanyahu’s standing ahead of what are expected to be punishing Israeli elections in October. He will be keeping an eye towards his domestic audience, even as he is expected to present a more staid image to the US public.

“Any opportunity he has to be photographed with Trump, the most powerful person in the world, is a personal political benefit to him,” Omer-Man said.

“He wants to emphasise his relationship with Trump, and he’s gonna argue that he’s the only one who knows how to deal with the US and the only one with the relationship with Trump,” he said.

To be sure, there are ways the meeting could backfire, Omer-Man assessed.

Trump could apply pressure related to a US-backed agreement between Lebanon and Israel, which is ostensibly aimed at Israel’s complete withdrawal from Lebanon, but appears to allow for the Israeli military’s near-indefinite occupation.

The US president could further assert pressure on the Trump-backed 20-point “peace plan” in Gaza, which has seen near-daily Israeli violations of the “ceasefire” in the enclave. Ahead of Netanyahu’s trip, the Israeli government approved the entry of an International Stabilization Force (ISF) in Gaza, although no timeframe was given for a more complete Israeli withdrawal.

The meeting also comes amid a virulent wave of settler violence in the occupied West Bank. Rights groups have long argued that such violence is not the result of rogue incidents, but is part of a direct government strategy.

Condemnation of settler attacks has become a rare, bipartisan cause in the US, including within the Trump administration.

“That could be the wild card here,” Omer-Man said. “As much as Trump has not wanted to antagonise or criticise or intervene in anything that Netanyahu or Israel has done or wanted to do, this is the one issue that has basically crossed all party lines in American politics in recent years.”

“It’s obviously heating up and looking pretty bad at the moment,” he said.

title: Sri Lanka finish strong to beat Pakistan 2-1 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
July.28 (Mirror Sports) - Chamari Athapaththu produced a captain's performance with both bat and ball as Sri Lanka defeated Pakistan by eight wickets in the third ODI on Tuesday to clinch the three-match series 2-1.

The Sri Lanka skipper claimed three wickets before blasting a 38-ball 52, while Harshitha Samarawickrama (71*) and Hasini Perera (50*) guided the hosts to 191-2 after Pakistan were dismissed for 187.

Sri Lanka's victory was set up by Chethana Vimukthi, who ripped through Pakistan's top order in a sensational second over. The seamer dismissed Sadaf Shamas, Sidra Amin and Ayesha Zafar in the space of five deliveries to leave the visitors reeling at 10-3.

Pakistan recovered through a 68-run stand between Gull Feroza and Muneeba Ali, with Feroza striking 40 off 35 balls before Athapaththu broke the partnership. Muneeba added 34, while captain Fatima Sana top-scored with 41, but regular wickets prevented Pakistan from building any lasting momentum.

Athapaththu and Kavisha Dilhari finished with three wickets each alongside Vimukthi as Sri Lanka bowled Pakistan out for 187.

In reply, Sri Lanka made a brisk start despite losing Vishmi Gunaratne for 12 after an opening stand of 46. Athapaththu then took control, bringing up her 20th ODI half-century during a fluent knock that featured aggressive strokeplay.

After the captain departed for 52, Samarawickrama and Hasini ensured there were no further setbacks. The pair shared an unbeaten 106-run partnership for the third wicket to steer Sri Lanka home comfortably.

Samarawickrama anchored the chase with an unbeaten 71, while Hasini reached her fifty in the closing stages as Sri Lanka completed the chase with ease.

Samarawickrama was named Player of the Series after scoring 173 runs, including a century in the second ODI, while Athapaththu collected the Player of the Match award for her outstanding all-round display.

The two sides will now shift their focus to the T20I series, which gets underway on Friday.

title: Charith Abeysinghe remanded after failing to meet bail conditions - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 28 (Daily Mirror) - Former Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) Horana organiser Charith Abeysinghe was remanded once again after failing to satisfy the bail conditions imposed by the Colombo Magistrate’s Court.

The court earlier granted bail to three suspects, including attorney Rakhitha Rajapaksha and Abeysinghe, who had been remanded over allegations of accepting a Rs. 120 million bribe from the wife of alleged underworld figure and suspected drug trafficker “Harak Kata”.

Attorney Rajapaksha and the third suspect were released after fulfilling the bail conditions.

However, Abeysinghe was taken back into remand custody after he failed to meet the conditions required for his release.

title: No plans as yet to restrict water supply despite dry conditions: NWSDB - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 28 (Daily Mirror) - The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has said there are no plans as yet to impose water supply restrictions in any part of the country despite the prevailing El Niño-related climate conditions.

According to NWSDB Chairman Chandana Bandara, the board is continuing operations at maximum water production capacity as no restrictions have been imposed on water extraction from major reservoirs by the Department of Irrigation or the Mahaweli Authority of Sri Lanka.

He said any decision to introduce water supply restrictions in the future would depend on changes in weather patterns, reservoir levels and instructions from relevant authorities.

“If water levels decline significantly and the Irrigation Department or the Mahaweli Authority are required to limit water withdrawals, the NWSDB will consider introducing restrictions based on the situation at that time,” Bandara said.

He added that the NWSDB has already begun preparations to face possible challenges arising from the prevailing climate conditions, including improving existing tube well systems to increase groundwater extraction.

Bandara urged the public to use water responsibly, avoid wastage and limit consumption to essential needs until the situation improves.

title: France evacuates 4,000 as Gironde wildfire faces renewed heat threat - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
INDIA TODAY - French authorities ordered nearly 4,000 people to evacuate tourist sites on the Atlantic coast on Tuesday as returning heat threatened firefighters’ fragile hold on a vast wildfire west of Bordeaux. The new evacuations added to a wildfire crisis across south-western Europe, where fires in France and Spain have forced about 330,000 people to leave their homes and holiday accommodation.

In France, officials said the Gironde fire had been stabilised but not fixed, meaning it could spread again as temperatures rise and humidity falls. In neighbouring Landes, thousands of evacuees were allowed to return after a separate wildfire was brought under control. In Spain, firefighters continued battling several major fires as the country entered its fourth heatwave of the summer.

Firefighters held the Gironde blaze in check through a calm night, controlling flare-ups near coastal dunes and keeping the burned area unchanged at 420 square kilometres. The precautionary evacuation order covered campsites, holiday villages, tourist residences and leisure parks around the resort of Lacanau, including Lacanau Ocean and both shores of Lacanau lake, regional authorities said.

“We are at a point of fragility,” Eric Brocardi, spokesperson for France’s national firefighters federation, told BFMTV on Tuesday. “We will continue attacking this fire despite the forecast rise in temperatures.” The fire, burning since last week, has at times turned into a self-feeding firestorm as it spread across an area four times the size of Paris and forced 220,000 people to evacuate.

Officials said that even after 24 hours without further spread, smouldering vegetation, rising temperatures and falling humidity could trigger fresh outbreaks along the vast perimeter. Firefighters and military engineers resumed work early on Tuesday on tactical firebreaks meant to stop the flames from spreading, with authorities saying 103 kilometres of firebreaks had been completed. The prefecture said 93 firefighters had been injured while battling the blaze. The A63 motorway remained partly closed, while rail traffic south of Bordeaux was suspended except on the route towards Toulouse.

The overnight progress in Gironde stood in contrast with clearer gains in Landes, where authorities said a separate wildfire had been fixed and more than 15,000 people were allowed to return home on Monday night in Sanguinet, Parentis-en-Born and parts of Biscarrosse. Residents of Biscarrosse’s aviation village and a large campsite were among those allowed back, though several other neighbourhoods remained out of bounds. “The fire is fixed, which is good news in the Landes,” French President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday evening. Authorities warned that the fire there had not been extinguished and that hot spots, wind and drought could still cause flare-ups for days or even weeks.

Both French fire zones faced a fresh test as temperatures started rising again on Tuesday. France’s national weather service placed Gironde under a yellow heat warning from midday, forecasting inland temperatures of 33 to 35C. South-east winds were expected across the department, along with westerly sea breezes on the coast. According to the Interior Ministry, more than 116,000 hectares have burned across France so far this year. The European Union’s Copernicus climate service said western Europe recorded its hottest June on record, with extreme heat and widespread dryness helping fires spread and intensify in France and Spain.

In Spain, hundreds of firefighters, backed by military emergency brigades and water-dropping aircraft, continued battling several major wildfires, including the largest ever recorded in the country. Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said nonstop work through the night left him “reasonably positive”, but he warned that conditions could worsen as temperatures rose again. Spain’s national weather service said the country was entering its fourth heatwave of the summer, with temperatures expected to cross 40C in some areas.

Authorities in Spain have evacuated about 79,000 people and ordered another 30,000 to remain in their homes during a crisis that led the government to declare a national emergency for wildfires for the first time. The biggest concern remained two large fires in wooded hills about an hour’s drive west of Madrid that had at times nearly merged into a single mega-blaze. Another fire in the eastern province of Castellƒón also forced mass evacuations.

A fire burning through hilly rural terrain in vila, west of Madrid, has become Spain’s largest on record, scorching more than 500 square kilometres, the government said. That is five times the size of Barcelona. “Look at how the valley is burned. Look at the houses, the people,” said David Gonzalez, a 48-year-old gardener who used his van to deliver supplies to firefighters in vila. “We are feeling a lot of anger and helplessness. It’s something inhuman,” he said.

Spain’s Ecology Minister Sara Aagesen said fires have burned 1,530 square kilometres in the country this year, six times the area scorched by blazes in the first half of 2025. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has called for a national pact to fight wildfires worsened by climate change. Across France and Spain, authorities were trying to hold the line as heat, wind and drought continued to threaten fresh flare-ups.

title: Sri Lanka to introduce rules for virtual assets, crypto firms - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 28 (Daily Mirror) - As the government seeks to strengthen supervision of Sri Lanka’s emerging digital asset sector, the Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to establish a legal framework for regulating virtual assets and virtual asset service providers (VASPs).

The proposal was presented by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in his capacity as Minister of Digital Economy, with the aim of introducing regulations to govern the use of virtual assets, including cryptocurrencies.

The proposed framework is expected to provide greater oversight of virtual asset activities, address risks linked to financial crimes, and ensure that service providers operate within a regulated environment.

title: India summons top Meta executive after PM Modi’s video briefly blocked - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Indian EXPRESS - The government has summoned Meta’s public policy chief after a video posted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi was briefly removed by Facebook in India, sources said. The video in question was uploaded by PM Modi last week – at the height of the Cockroach Janta Party’s protest against leaked exam papers.

In the video the PM assured protesters his government would pass a tough new law with stricter penalties for those found guilty of such acts.

“Friends, I am well aware that the issue of paper leaks is not a small matter. It causes immense distress to lakhs of students and their parents. Consequently, numerous measures have been taken over the past two-and-a-half months following these incidents, and the culprits have been apprehended and are currently in jail,” Modi said in the video.

“Working tirelessly, late into the night, the departments have already submitted a draft proposal to me. This draft, which includes provisions for fast-track courts and stricter penalties, will be discussed in the Cabinet tomorrow. It will be finalised after incorporating suggestions from Cabinet colleagues, and efforts will be made to pass the Bill in the House as soon as possible, starting with the second week of the Parliament’s session this coming Monday,” he said.

Meta said the video had been removed in error and has since been restored.

Queries to the Ministry of Information Technology were unanswered at publication.

Shot vertically, the video was seen by many as PM Modi trying to communicate with young people via social media platforms like Instagram, where shorter videos in that format are popular.

After the CJP-led protests wound down last week – once Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as the Education Minister – the government branded some videos and photographs of the agitation ‘objectionable’ and ordered them to be removed from popular social media platforms, including Facebook.

These included videos with derogatory references to senior government figures.

Meta – which owns popular social media platforms like Instagram, WhatsApp, and Facebook – has been in the government’s crosshairs over the past few weeks, and the CJP’s NEET exam paper leak protests have intensified that spotlight.

A significant amount of commentary and documentation surrounding the protest happened primarily on Instagram.

Before that the app was under fire over distribution of child sexual abuse material on the platform.

WhatsApp, also owned by Meta, faces scrutiny over its proposed ‘usernames’ feature.

Earlier this month the government asked the popular messaging service to not roll out that feature amid concerns of impersonation and fraud. In a notice to the company, the IT Ministry gave WhatsApp three days to furnish a response.

In its notice, the government is understood to have told WhatsApp that the feature may materially increase the incidence of online fraud, phishing, digital arrest scams and impersonation attacks, by enabling bad actors to solicit and message unsuspecting users. The government has also flagged that the feature may facilitate impersonation of individuals, public authorities, financial institutions and government agencies, by permitting the adoption of usernames closely resembling those of genuine people and institutions.

title: Sri Lankan gets 89 days in Australian prison for train assault - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
July 28 (Daily Mirror) - A 22-year-old Sri Lankan man has been sentenced to 89 days in prison by an Australian court for assaulting a fellow passenger with a glass bottle aboard a train in Brisbane.

The man, whose identity has not been disclosed, was convicted after striking an unidentified person on the head with a glass bottle during the incident on a Brisbane commuter train.

The Australian court imposed an immediate custodial sentence, describing the assault as a serious offence. He was ordered to serve 89 days in prison, just under three months.

Australian authorities treat violent offences on public transport seriously due to the risks posed to passengers in confined spaces. Queensland's public transport network is monitored by police and transit officers, with CCTV footage often used in investigations.

No further details have been released regarding the victim's condition or the circumstances that led to the assault.

title: Cabinet approves drug law reforms to expedite disposal - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 28 (Daily Mirror) - The Cabinet of Ministers has approved amendments to the Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance to enable the speedy disposal of confiscated narcotics and strengthen legal provisions relating to drug offences.

The proposed amendments will establish a legal framework allowing authorities to destroy confiscated narcotics without having to retain them until the conclusion of court proceedings. The new provisions will also apply to future drug seizures.

The move follows Cabinet approval granted on March 16, 2026, to amend the Ordinance based on the recommendations of a committee appointed to review the existing legal framework.

The Cabinet has also approved further amendments to Sections 54(1)(a) and 83(2), as well as the Third Schedule of the Ordinance, to strengthen provisions relating to the production and possession of dangerous drugs on the high seas. The changes take into account the provisions introduced under the Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Act No. 7 of 2026.

Accordingly, the Cabinet approved a proposal submitted by the Minister of Justice and National Integration to publish the amendment Bill, already drafted by the Legal Draftsman, in the Government Gazette before presenting it to Parliament for approval.

title: Major quake in southern Japan knocks out power, disrupts transport
summary: An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.1 struck Japan’s southern Kumamoto prefecture on Tuesday, knocking out power to thousands of homes, snarling travel and triggering evacuation orders and warnings for aftershocks.

title: LPL 2026 Playoff Race Heats Up - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Updated at 03.36 p.m.

July.28 (Mirror Sports) - The Lanka Premier League 2026 has entered its decisive phase, with six league matches remaining before the playoffs. Galle Gallants lead the points table after 14 matches, while Colombo Kaps and Jaffna Kings remain firmly in contention. Dambulla Sixers and Kandy Royals are also in the hunt, making every remaining fixture crucial in the battle for the top four.

Kandy Royals' Lahiru Udara leads the Orange Cap race with 222 runs, while teammate Nuwan Thushara tops the Purple Cap standings with 11 wickets. The top four teams will qualify for the playoffs, which begin on August 5 at the R. Premadasa International Cricket Stadium in Colombo. The LPL 2026 final is scheduled for August 8.
